notes.text: Session mode string comparison is NOT CASESPECIFIC and ignores trailing blanks. segment = 'silver' becomes lower(rtrim(segment,' ')) = lower(rtrim('silver',' ')). Without this, a plain DuckDB = misses variants like 'Silver' and 'SILVER ' (33 rows instead of 99 on dataset A).

Teradata TRIM(x) removes only leading and trailing spaces, so it maps to DuckDB trim(x, ' ') with the space character written out. The legacy table keeps the original cust_code casing, so no case folding is applied to it. Output types are cust_id INTEGER, cust_code VARCHAR, signup_date DATE, the same as the legacy output.

Session-mode NOT CASESPECIFIC, blank-padded comparison: status IN ('pending','Shipped') matches 'Pending ', 'SHIPPED ', 'shipped' etc. in Teradata. Rewritten as lower(rtrim(status)) IN (lower(rtrim('pending')), lower(rtrim('Shipped'))) so that both the column and the literals are normalised.

Session-mode string comparison: channel = 'WEB' is NOT CASESPECIFIC and blank-padded in Teradata, so it matches 'web', 'Web  ', etc. DuckDB '=' is case- and space-sensitive; rewritten as lower(rtrim(channel)) = lower(rtrim('WEB')).

Session mode NOT CASESPECIFIC, blank-padded comparisons: join ol.sku (CHAR(10)) = p.sku and filter p.category = 'garden' rewritten as lower(rtrim(a)) = lower(rtrim(b)) on both sides, so trailing spaces and case differences match as in Teradata.

ZEROIFNULL(credit_limit) is Teradata-only; mapped to COALESCE(credit_limit, 0) in both the output column and the CASE band test, so NULL limits become 0 and fall into 'LOW'. Cast explicitly to DECIMAL(12,2) to keep the legacy column type. No string comparisons, rounding, division or ORDER BY in this script, so no other session-mode semantics apply.

INTEGER / INTEGER truncates toward zero in Teradata; DuckDB '/' returns DOUBLE. Used integer '//' (verified it rounds toward zero for negatives: -7//2 = -3, 7//-2 = -3), cast to BIGINT to match the legacy output type. COUNT(*) >= 1 per group, so division by zero can't happen; if every total_items in a group is NULL, the result is NULL on both platforms.

Teradata sorts NULLs first in ASC. The window ORDER BY (ship_date ASC, order_id ASC) now says NULLS FIRST on both keys, so a customer whose orders include one with a NULL ship_date gets that order as its "first" row, as in legacy (149 of 266 legacy rows have a non-null ship_date). DuckDB's default is NULLS LAST, which would pick a different row. The partition key cust_id is INTEGER, so no case or trailing-space comparison rules apply.

The job is meant to find each customer's first order "in fulfilment order". Because Teradata sorts NULLs first, an order that has not shipped (NULL ship_date) beats every shipped order. On dataset A, 117 of 266 customers get an unshipped order as their first shipment. This is reproduced for parity and not fixed.

DATE - DATE: in Teradata this gives an integer number of days. In DuckDB, subtracting two DATE values also gives an integer day count (BIGINT), so run_date - MAX(order_date) is kept as is and cast explicitly to BIGINT to match the legacy column type. The script has no string comparisons (cust_id is INTEGER), no rounding, no division and no ORDER BY, so the other session-mode rules do not apply here. If MAX(order_date) is NULL, days_since is NULL and lapsed falls to 0, the same as in Teradata.
